original.target_description: Experiment 3: main effect of smiley use on perceived competence, across formal and informal contexts, two-way ANCOVA controlling for participant gender.

n.sample_role: Participants in the gender-adjusted 2 × 2 ANCOVA; final sample after attention exclusions.
n.exclusions: 92 recruited; seven excluded for failing an attention question.
n.location: Article p. 7 / published p. 620, Participants and Design; ANCOVA on article p. 8 / published p. 621.

es.location: Article p. 8 / published p. 621, Perceived Competence, smiley main effect.

p.location: Article p. 8 / published p. 621, Perceived Competence, smiley main effect.

replication.target_description: Replication: main effect of smiley use on perceived competence, across formal and informal contexts, two-way ANCOVA controlling for participant gender.

n.sample_role: Participants in gender-adjusted ANCOVA, not the full final sample of 847.
n.exclusions: 1002 complete responses; excluded completion under one minute (n = 129) or non-differentiated responses (n = 34), leaving 847. A further 24 not reporting male/female gender were excluded for gender-adjusted analyses. Manipulation-check failures were retained in this analysis.
n.location: p. 4, Analysis and Results; p. 2, Participants and Design.

es.location: p. 5, Perceived Competence, gender-adjusted smiley main effect.

p.location: p. 5, Perceived Competence, gender-adjusted smiley main effect.

reported_success.location: p. 5, Perceived Competence, opening sentence referring to the negative smiley main effect.

notes: Target is the smiley main effect on competence; the supplied description does not restrict the effect to a context. Author-printed d and p are retained, including the original paper’s printed F/p combination, without recalculation. Replication d is an author-reported conversion. Narrative success is limited to this main effect; the replication did not reproduce the context interaction or moderated mediation.
